leftEvidence.title: Famine reaches Saul’s violence and Rizpah’s vigil

points.label: Action and response
points.left: David inquires about a three-year famine, hears a charge concerning Saul and Gibeon, hands over seven descendants, while Rizpah guards the bodies until rain and David gathers bones for burial.
points.right: David grows faint against a Philistine giant, Abishai saves him, and the men swear that he will no longer go out lest Israel’s lamp be quenched; further giant battles are listed.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places inherited violence, public death, maternal vigil, burial, rain, and answered prayer remain in one difficult sequence inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places the warrior king becomes someone whose life others protect inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Samuel 21:1–14 and 2 Samuel 21:15–22 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Famine, Song, Last Words, and Census” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

payload.tension: 2 Samuel 21:1–14 foregrounds inherited violence, public death, maternal vigil, burial, rain, and answered prayer remain in one difficult sequence; 2 Samuel 21:15–22 foregrounds the warrior king becomes someone whose life others protect. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
